imagePrompt: A teenage left-handed girl with a wedge accidentally double-hits the golf ball during a chip shot on the sunny fairway, wearing a red top, white bottoms, and a hat.
imageAlt: A girl golfer chips the ball and accidentally hits it twice in one swing.

issues: The only minor issue is that the left-handed posture could be shown more clearly by reversing hand position or stance more distinctly; currently, it's not fully obvious for teaching left-handed grip, but not incorrect.
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Adjust the girl's golf grip and stance to make it even more clearly left-handed, showing her right hand lower on the shaft and stance matching a left-hander, while keeping all other details the same and accurate.

questions.title: What if my club hits the ball twice, but I only swung once?
questions.question: You try a hard chip shot, but your club taps the ball two times in the same swing. What should you do?

choices.text: Count two hits and add an extra penalty point
Count only one hit with no extra points
Count one hit and add an extra penalty point
Don’t count the shot; play again for free

questions.explanation: If you hit the ball twice but only took one swing, it just counts as one shot. You don’t get any extra penalty.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A short hit to make the ball go in the air and land on the green.
Extra points added for breaking a rule.

questions.teachingTip: You can show this with a slow-motion video or by having kids practise slow chip shots, so they see when the club might hit the ball more than once.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids may think you have to add extra points if the club taps the ball twice.
Some might feel like they need to replay the shot, but they do not.

questions.title: What happens if you accidentally hit the ball twice in one swing?
questions.question: During a tricky chip, your club accidentally hits the ball twice in the same swing. How many strokes do you count and is there a penalty?

choices.text: Count two strokes and add a penalty stroke
Count one stroke with no penalty
Count one stroke and add a penalty stroke
Ignore the shot and play again without penalty

questions.explanation: If you double-hit the ball in a single swing, it counts as just one stroke and there is no penalty.
